title: Profiling and Debugging Cache Behavior
description: Learn to measure cache hit ratios, diagnose common caching issues, and use profiling tools to optimize ASP.NET Core caching performance.

data.text: A cache that is incorrectly configured can be worse than no cache at all. Stale data confuses users, excessive TTLs waste memory, and poor hit ratios mean your application still hits the database on most requests. Profiling reveals whether caching is actually delivering value and where the bottlenecks are.

Start with the fundamental metric: cache hit ratio. A healthy in-memory or distributed cache should have a ratio above 80 percent for hot data. Below that, you are paying for infrastructure without getting most of the benefit. If the ratio is low, investigate the expiration settings, key design, and access patterns.

terms.definition: The percentage of cache requests that return a value. Calculated as hits / (hits + misses).
A sudden burst of cache misses that all try to repopulate the same entry at once, overloading the data source.
Synonymous with cache stampede. Also describes many clients retrying a failed backend simultaneously.
A statistical measure (p50, p95, p99) that shows typical and worst-case response times, including the time saved by caching.

data.text: MemoryCache exposes a Count property and the PostEvictionCallback event for coarse-grained monitoring. For production-grade metrics, wrap the cache in a decorator that records hits, misses, and latencies through your existing metrics system.

data.title: Decorating IMemoryCache with Metrics
data.content: Wrap the cache to collect hit and miss counts using System.Diagnostics.Metrics.

data.text: Profiling Redis with INFO and Monitoring Tools

Redis provides built-in observability through the INFO command, which returns server statistics including keyspace hits and misses. Calculate the hit ratio from these values and set up alerts when the ratio drops below your threshold.

data.title: Fetching Redis INFO via StackExchange.Redis
data.content: Query Redis INFO stats and compute the hit ratio from keyspace_hits and keyspace_misses.

data.title: Redis SLOWLOG
data.text: Redis maintains a slow log of commands that exceed a configurable threshold. Use SLOWLOG GET to identify cache operations that are unexpectedly slow — often caused by large value sizes or network issues.

items.text: Instrument both IMemoryCache and IDistributedCache with hit/miss counters
items.hint: Use a decorator pattern for IMemoryCache and Redis INFO for distributed cache

items.text: Set up dashboards showing hit ratio, p95 latency, and eviction counts
items.hint: Grafana + Prometheus or Application Insights are common choices

items.text: Configure Redis maxmemory-policy to evict least-recently-used keys
items.hint: volatile-lru or allkeys-lru are the most common eviction policies

items.text: Alert when hit ratio drops below 80 percent
Run Redis SLOWLOG regularly and tune slow command thresholds
items.hint: SLOWLOG GET and SLOWLOG RESET are your primary tools

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cache hit ratio above 80% is the standard health target
Wrap IMemoryCache in a decorator to collect metrics without modifying core code
Redis INFO and SLOWLOG provide built-in observability for distributed caches
Set up alerts on hit ratio drops and slow command spikes
Use dashboards (Grafana, Application Insights) to track cache health trends
data.takeaway: You cannot optimize what you do not measure. Profiling turns caching from a guess into a data-driven decision.
